[untitled BTM module] These genes form a brake system on leukocyte activation, tuning how strongly lymphocytes and myeloid cells respond to antigen receptor, Toll-like and cytokine receptor engagement. Restraint of this kind sets thresholds for activation, prevents autoimmunity and chronic inflammation, and is also what tumours exploit to blunt T cell responses, making several members attractive immunotherapy targets.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the myeloid identity and activation program of monocytes and macrophages, the cells that patrol tissue for microbes and debris and set the tone of an inflammatory response. The transcription factor SPI1 (PU.1) specifies this lineage together with HHEX, while TLR4 senses bacterial lipopolysaccharide and PTAFR responds to platelet-activating factor, coupling through the Src-family kinase LYN, the phospholipase PLCB2 and the ITAM-bearing adaptor TYROBP (DAP12) to calcium mobilization and cytoskeletal change; DOK2 acts as a brake on this kinase signaling.
